Dark Puissance represents your capital for seizing power within the Witch King's Black Tower of Naggarond\\n\\n[[col:yellow]][[img:icon_ghs_def_black_tower_rule]][[/img]]Dark Puissance can be earned through constructing buildings, faction mechanics, characters, and confederations, and can be converted into Slave resources via Slave Orders\\n\\n[[col:yellow]][[img:icon_ghs_def_black_tower_rule]][[/img]]In the Black Tower at the very heart of Naggarond, you can spend Dark Puissance to gain powerful rewards[[/col]]
We need Dark Puissance—defeat those ungrateful fools in the Witch King's Black Tower!
We need to keep control over the lives of our slaves; let us slow our encroachment on the Black Tower

The Witch King's Black Tower stands at the heart of Naggarond, a labyrinth of palaces, ramparts, and towers that brings wealth and prestigious honor. The Witch King has always been a capricious ruler—when fortune favors him, he can be exceedingly generous, but should things not go as he plans, he becomes immovably ruthless and cruel.
Some complacent Dread Lord dies never understanding just what reckless rebel dared to strike him down!
The defeated, high and low alike, are stripped of everything before being marched to the mines. We always find something novel among them.
Are you thinking what I'm thinking? The slave pens are nearly empty! For the pleasure of all Druchii, let the blood flow today!
There are never enough slaves. The mines' hunger for labor knows no end, and the Witch King's newest schemes will demand a fortune.
What pleasure there is in slicing through an enemy's defenses, gently opening a throat, and driving straight for the heart!
Momentum is the key to conquest, and only this seat can muster the resources needed to keep the armies marching.
Whoever holds the armory keys is trusted most by the Dread Lord, but that does not mean no one is watching his every move.
At the Black Tower Lord's summons, warriors gather from every corner.
Atop the Prophecy Tower of Ghrond, the sorceresses of the Dark Convent study the wicked sorceries of Chaos. Such energies can disturb the Great Vortex.
Those who can bend the Winds of Magic to the Witch King's will earn lofty station—and closer scrutiny.
To the Druchii, the scent of pain is the finest perfume, and no sound brings such despair as the twisted prophecies of a Medusa Oracle.
Spell-items forged from Druhir, or Black Magic, are among the most destructive. Their power is drawn from unrefined Winds of Magic, but the price the wielder pays is steep.
Master of slaves, whipmaster of shirkers, and the direct source of taxes for the Black Tower Lord.
The vast holds of the Black Ark carry slaves, bound either for Naggarond or for service to their cruel masters aboard ship.
Once again it is time for the Dark Elves to sail to distant shores for pillage and plunder! The mines of Naggaroth forever hunger for fresh flesh!
They need no one's aid, and danger means nothing to them—the only cure is to rejoice in slaughter to their heart's content.
Warriors who know nothing of mercy fight desperately for survival in the twisted streets of Naggaroth's cities; most of them are eventually conscripted.
Shadows can move like phantoms through petrified forests and jagged stone thickets—even by the Dark Elves' brutal standards, such a life is hell.
Competition for rank within the Dark Convent is bloody and fierce; only those who survive their own ambition are fortunate enough to learn the world's most powerful magic.
The White Tower elves who fancy themselves masters of the Winds of Magic never suspect that every incantation they utter is heard clearly by ears in the dark.
The ancient archives of Ghrond hold many secrets that can save a life... or take one.
The corrupt and malevolent Midnight of Death demands sacrifice. If we offer up... an offering, perhaps the gods can be appeased?
Beaten, starved, and kept at their posts without rest, slaves are wrung of every last drop of labor.
The High Elves cast the Dark Elves out; the two peoples are now utterly distinct, brother turned against brother, a rift beyond mending, each harboring hatred for the other.
Malekith's life is sustained by dark power alone; the Witch King has sworn to witness with his own eyes the last Phoenix King's end—and even should heaven and earth crumble, he will wait!
Death walks with all who master the Winds of Magic, and those who command the power of the Wind of Shyish are, without question, more skilled than most in the art of killing.
Most sorceresses lurk in utter darkness, using illusions to conjure cruel visions to deceive their prey, seizing the souls they crave.
